A live star is not a recipe. Every second the Eye updates a §9stability field§r. At T1 it has one gauge, §9P§r (pressure balance): minus is collapse, plus is expansion, and§9 0 is the target§r. Each higher star adds a gauge.

§5§lZONES§r The worst gauge sets the zone, the yield and Integrity:
- §9Resonant§r within ±10: yield ×1.25, Integrity +1 a second
- §2Stable§r within ±40: ×1.00, +0.2
- §5Strained§r within ±70: ×0.50, −0.5
- §cCritical§r within ±100: no yield, −2
- §4Breach§r beyond ±100: the star is lost at once
§9Integrity§r (0-100) at 0 also loses the star. A lost star costs the star and its unfinished cycle, §lnever§r blocks, cores or unlocked tiers. Relight it with a new charge.

§5§lTRIM§r Pour trim fluids into the §9Field sockets§r: 8 plain input hatches on the core band. They are never buffered, and ME stocking hatches there are refused. At T1, 1,000 L Helium is §9P −2§r and 1,000 L Hydrogen is §9P +2§r, up to 10 units a second.

§5§lSENSE§r A §9Stellar Field Sensor Hatch§r (8 sockets on the core band) reads one channel against a threshold and emits redstone on all sides: digital (15 above or below the threshold) or analog (0-15 across the range). Channels: P, Θ, Ω, Π, the Agent shield, Integrity, Stability, zone, event warning (+, − or any) and upkeep OK. Right-click it to set it up.

§5§lAUTOMATE§r The standard rig:
- a sensor on §9P > +10§r → a Fluid Regulator cover, or an ME fluid export bus with a redstone card → Helium into a Field hatch;
- a second sensor on §9P < −10§r → Hydrogen.
Covers on the sensor's own side work, wireless redstone transmitters included, so one sensor can drive a valve anywhere.

[note]Sol settles at about P +35 (Stable) by itself, so T1 runs unattended; the rig earns the ×1.25. Higher stars do §lnot§r settle. A §9Directive Hatch§r in a sensor socket gives the whole rig as one binary code instead, and OpenComputers (bts_eye) can drive it too.[/note]

§2§lDONE §lWHEN§r you hold a sensor hatch. Here is a second one for the rig.
